messages.subject: Re: MacOS X 10.11 El Capitan broke Stat-ET?
messages.subject_clean: MacOS X 10.11 El Capitan broke Stat-ET?
messages.body_plain:
Ok, this was a pain in the butt to fix.  If anyone else had StatET break
after the El Capitan install, here is how I had to fix it:

1) Install this: https://support.apple.com/kb/DL1572?locale=en_US

2) Install Xcode from the App Store, and then download/install the latest
Command Line Tools (OS X 10.11 -- NOTE THE OS VERSION) from
https://developer.apple.com/downloads/ (you will need an account).  As of
today it is listed as beta 3.  This properly installs the JRI headers where
they need to go.  These were missing for some reason.  This will eventually
show up on the App Store, but it isn't there yet.

3) Fire up a Terminal window.  Type the following:
/usr/libexec/java_home -V
You should see something like:

 1.8.0_60, x86_64: "Java SE 8"
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home

    1.8.0_20, x86_64: "Java SE 8"
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_20.jdk/Contents/Home

    1.6.0_65-b14-468, x86_64: "Java SE 6"
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/1.6.0.jdk/Contents/Home
    1.6.0_65-b14-468, i386: "Java SE 6"
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/1.6.0.jdk/Contents/Home

4) Pick the latest and greatest (I guess?  Try other ones if this doesn't
work) version number...  You might want to install the latest JDK for MacOS
X from Oracle if you only have 1.6, OR if you don't see anything with "jdk"
above.

5)  Type:
export JAVA_HOME=`/usr/libexec/java_home -v 1.8.0_60`
(Swap in the version number as needed above from step #2)
6) R CMD javareconf

IMPORTANT: you should see something like this at the top.
Java interpreter :
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home/jre/bin/java
Java version     : 1.8.0_60
Java home path   :
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home
Java compiler    :
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/javac
Java headers gen.:
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/javah
Java archive tool:
/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk1.8.0_60.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/jar
System Java on OS X

7) You should be able to install rj and rj.gd now from the GUI or R command
line:
install.packages(c("rj", "rj.gd"), repos="http://download.walware.de/rj-2.0
")

8) Confirm it works again in Eclipse.

If anyone has any suggestions for how to mod this, please let me know!
Good luck!

--j

messages.body_plain:
hi, can anyone help with this problem regarding R-help?

OS X Yosemite
Jave 1.8
R3.2
Eclipse LUNA
StatET  version 3.4.2.b201506120830E44sw
rj_2.0.4-2

problems:
1. At the console, ?read.table leads to a page "No help found"
2. If I hover the cursor to a function name, it popup a small yellow
window, but only showing the function header, not complete info as in R
documentation.

I appreciate any help!

Thanks,
Jack

messages.subject: Re: problems with R-help
messages.body_plain:
I found the problem. In Mac, the default R_HOME is

*/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources*

*However, seems it's just a softlink. After I changed it to *
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources

Everything worked.
